canonical_exact_scope: Fix an actual Alexander population P avoiding an infinite label word s. For every countable family of actual population hosts U_j, there is one positive finite-fibre terminal clone Q of a one-parent-per-label selection of P such that Q avoids s, its actual roots are canonically equivalent to P's, and every nonroot has exactly one incoming parent of every label. Every infinite word realized by Q is realized by P. For every j, every finite global stretch L and every injective map Q→U_j, some source edge does not map to an undirected host path of length at most L. Hosts need not avoid s or have exact parent counts. The actual population assumptions are infinitude, real chronological birthdates with finite birth sublevels, finitely many roots and children per vertex, functional edge labels and parent coverage at each nonroot. Parent selection can shrink the original language; terminal cloning preserves the selected language exactly. For an already exact-parent P, cloning preserves the whole original language. There is no uniform child cap, no terminal-free condition and no uncountable-host or unbounded-stretch conclusion.
